newsitem.title: UK: Green rate inspires UK rush to EU grain tender.
newsitem.headline: Green rate inspires UK rush to EU grain tender.

text.p: A likely sterling green rate revaluation on January 21 triggered larger than usual interest from British grain exporters in Thursday's EU open market tender, traders said.
A revaluation would cut the value of the export refund in sterling terms, so there was an obvious potential advantage in obtaining export licences before any change.
So-called green rates are used by the EU to convert export refunds, set in Ecu, into the national currencies of its member states.
Analysts at the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority currently predict a revaluation to 0.769374 sterling per ECU, reflecting the UK unit's continued relative strength against other European currencies.
The HGCA's calculations are done on the basis of official ECU rates issued each afternoon.
Green rates are changed under a system based around the 10-day average of the value of a currency against the Ecu.

This means that that the 14.90 Ecu per tonne refund awarded by the EU grains management committee is equivalent to some 12.07 stg. But if the committee were to award the same level at its next meeting, on January 23 the likely level of refund for UK exporters would be 11.46 stg.

It looks as though UK exporters got more than 50,000 tonnes worth of licences in Thursday's tender. So somebody has saved around 3,000 stg. According to the UK's Intervention Board for Agricultural Produce there were fewer than three bidders for licences in the UK.
There is no other reason for the rush, traders said. "It's purely technical," one said. "If you need licences this was the time to get them."
